correctness.rationale: The frozen complete-cycle law is valid: normalizing the OU endpoint conditional on its exponential duration gives an independent standard normal, U=e^(−2μT) has CDF u^β, and E=(1−U)Z²/2. Conditional Gaussian integration gives the frozen moment criterion (the critical integral is β∫₀¹u^(β−3/2)du); a Mills bound and the scaling v=wU give the tail and conditional gamma law. Selection of the maximum over iid pairs multiplies the exact joint density by n(1−S)^(n−1), which also checks the independent limit and the frozen age scale. The duration maximum has order log n, and even its selected normal mark is standard normal because the duration vector is independent of all normal marks. The repaired RESULT.md additionally proves a local joint-density correction. After wU=z, the Gaussian-tail multiplier has first coefficient −z/2−z²−1/2; integrating against Gamma(β,1) gives −κ(β+1). Split at z=w/2 and bound the Taylor error by an integrable polynomial times w^(−2), with the rest exponentially small. The exact quantile nS(b_n)=1 therefore gives nS(b_n+x)=e^(−x)[1−κx/b_n+O(b_n^(−2))]. Expanding the exact winner density then gives the recorded joint coefficient and compact-uniform remainder. As a separate sign check the logarithm of the four-point density ratio is exactly −(x1−x2)[(1−v1/b_n)^(−1)−(1−v2/b_n)^(−1)] when all four points are in the support. The limiting density has unit mass, giving total-variation convergence by Scheffé. The supplied finite checks concern the frozen one-cycle identities and tail; no uploaded scripts were used to establish the new expansion.
